title: Network intrusion
note: REAL data (lab testbed) — intrusion=1. RT-IoT2022 — DOI 10.24432/C5P338, CC BY 4.0: real network flows (Zeek + Flowmeter) captured on a real IoT testbed — ThingSpeak-LED, Wipro bulb and MQTT temperature-sensor traffic as normal, and attacks STAGED by the researchers with standard tools (hping3 SYN flood, Slowloris, Nmap scans, ARP poisoning, Metasploit SSH brute force); lab traffic, not a production network. Held-out = by capture order inside each scenario, case mix 25.00% positive (population 89.81%); grown only on the training split.
lineage: Grown by tools/build-real-brains.mjs with src/grow.mjs growPattern — the seed-library ribosome (sjgant80-hub/seed-library, vendored) — on the training split only, graded once on the held-out split. Pattern shape and answer path: the Konomi SLM (sjgant80-hub/konomi-slm). Konomi architecture: Thomas Frumkin.

provenance.citation: B. S. Sharmila and Rohini Nagapadma. RT-IoT2022 [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository, 2023. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5P338 — described in "Quantized autoencoder (QAE) intrusion detection system for anomaly detection in resource-constrained IoT devices using RT-IoT2022 dataset", Cybersecurity (2023)
provenance.label: intrusion=1: the flow belongs to a staged attack (Attack_type is anything other than MQTT_Publish, Thing_Speak or Wipro_bulb)
provenance.split: by capture order inside each scenario — for every traffic type the first 70% of its flows (by the published per-scenario index, after de-duplication) are the training split and the last 30% the held-out split
